policy: Projects generate evidence and transfer opportunities; completion is not mastery. Adapt scope, materials and supervision to age and context.

projects.title: Build a small digital product with evidence of real usefulness
projects.challenge: Design and test a narrowly scoped digital product or service for a clearly defined user problem without assuming demand.
deliverables: decision memo: continue, change or stop
phases: Separate observation from assumptions; conduct consent-based discovery.
Define one user task and measurable acceptance criteria.
Build the smallest testable prototype and document versions.
Calculate direct costs, time capacity and break-even scenarios with assumptions.
Test usability, privacy and failure cases using dummy data.
Present findings, uncertainty and a justified next decision.
acceptance_criteria: At least one user task is testable end-to-end.
Claims about demand are limited to collected evidence.
Calculations reconcile and assumptions are visible.
No real sensitive user data is required.
A failure or stop decision is treated as valid evidence.

rubric.problem_evidence: 0–3: from unsupported assumption to traceable, appropriately limited user evidence
rubric.technical_quality: 0–3: from nonfunctional to tested prototype with documented limits
rubric.quantitative_reasoning: 0–3: from missing arithmetic to reconciled scenarios and sensitivity checks
rubric.responsibility: 0–3: from ignored risks to proportionate privacy, security and ethical safeguards

projects.safety_ethics: Use dummy/test data; obtain guardian approval for public release or spending; no deceptive marketing, scraping or unauthorised testing.
projects.transfer_test: Repeat the same discovery and evaluation method for a different user group; explain which method transferred and which assumptions did not.

projects.title: Low-voltage sensor investigation and engineering notebook
projects.challenge: Investigate a simple low-voltage sensor or circuit using predictions, controlled measurements and clear reporting.
phases: Define a narrow question and identify variables.
Select a documented beginner-safe low-voltage setup.
Predict behaviour using appropriate circuit models.
Build only with suitable supervision and verified components.
Measure, record instrument limitations and compare predictions.
Explain deviations without hiding inconvenient results.
acceptance_criteria: Circuit and power source remain within documented safe limits.
Diagram, units and observations are reproducible.
At least one alternative explanation is considered.
Conclusions match the evidence and stated limitations.

rubric.model: 0–3: from absent to justified prediction with assumptions
rubric.measurement: 0–3: from untraceable to repeatable records with units
rubric.communication: 0–3: from unclear to independently reproducible explanation

projects.safety_ethics: No mains electricity, exposed high-energy sources, lithium battery modification or unsupervised soldering; adult supervision and known-safe kit required.
projects.transfer_test: Apply the same prediction-measurement-revision cycle to a non-electrical physical investigation.

projects.title: Research a claim and publish a bilingual evidence explainer
projects.challenge: Evaluate a public claim and explain what the evidence does and does not establish in accessible Bangla and English.
phases: Turn a broad claim into a bounded answerable question.
Search for primary and authoritative sources where appropriate.
Compare methods, sample, date, conflicts and limitations.
Check numerical claims and distinguish correlation from causation.
Draft both language versions with consistent meaning.
Test comprehension and revise confusing or overstated statements.
acceptance_criteria: Every material factual claim has traceable provenance.
Uncertainty and disagreement are represented fairly.
Bangla and English versions preserve the same substantive meaning.
A reader can correctly explain the main conclusion after reading.

rubric.source_quality: 0–3: from unsupported to diverse, relevant and traceable sources
rubric.quantitative_interpretation: 0–3: from misread to contextually correct with limitations
rubric.bilingual_fidelity: 0–3: from inconsistent to accurate equivalent meaning
rubric.audience_comprehension: 0–3: from untested to reader-tested and revised

projects.safety_ethics: Avoid private individuals, medical diagnosis, political targeting or exposing personal information; distinguish educational information from professional advice.
projects.transfer_test: Evaluate a second claim from a different field and identify which source-evaluation principles remain valid.

projects.title: Football performance: observe, analyse, practise, reassess
projects.challenge: Analyse one football skill or decision using observations, then design a safe practice intervention and reassess.
phases: Choose one observable behaviour, not a vague goal.
Record a small baseline sample and separate decision quality from outcome.
Identify plausible technical, tactical and contextual factors.
Design a manageable practice constraint with rest and stop signals.
Reassess using comparable observations and note confounders.
acceptance_criteria: Measures are defined before practice.
No claim of causation from a tiny uncontrolled sample.
Training load is age-appropriate and includes recovery.
Pain, dizziness, unusual breathlessness or injury triggers stopping and adult support.

rubric.observation: 0–3: from impression to repeatable, specific records
rubric.analysis: 0–3: from outcome bias to contextual explanation and uncertainty
rubric.practice_design: 0–3: from unsafe/unfocused to safe, specific and progressive
rubric.reflection: 0–3: from anecdote to comparison and next-step rationale

projects.safety_ethics: No maximal testing, weight-loss targets, punishment conditioning or training through pain; adapt to weather, surface and supervision.
projects.transfer_test: Apply observation → hypothesis → intervention → reassessment to a non-sport learning or workflow task.

projects.title: Create an accessible visual story with recorded narration
projects.challenge: Create a short visual sequence and narration that communicate one idea clearly to a defined audience.
phases: Define the message and audience.
Develop several visual compositions before choosing one.
Use contrast, sequence, pacing and readable typography intentionally.
Prepare clear narration with appropriate diction and vocal care.
Add captions/alt description and test comprehension.
Revise based on specific audience feedback.
acceptance_criteria: Sequence is understandable without relying only on decorative polish.
Narration is intelligible and does not strain the voice.
Text and visual contrast are usable on a phone.
At least one revision responds to observed confusion.

rubric.visual_structure: 0–3: from confusing to coherent intentional sequence
rubric.performance: 0–3: from unclear/strained to intelligible and sustainable
rubric.iteration: 0–3: from no revision to evidence-led revision

projects.safety_ethics: Use licensed or original assets; obtain consent for identifiable voices/images; avoid harmful imitation or unsafe vocal strain.
projects.transfer_test: Reuse the audience-testing method in a non-artistic information design task.

projects.title: Household systems and hazard-aware independence audit
projects.challenge: Improve one low-risk household routine while documenting cost, clarity, safety boundaries and escalation points.
deliverables: reflection on what should remain unchanged
phases: Choose a reversible, low-risk task with guardian agreement.
Observe the current process without collecting private data.
Identify hazards and stop/escalation conditions.
Redesign instructions and calculate relevant quantities.
Trial the change under appropriate supervision.
Review whether the change genuinely helped.
acceptance_criteria: No high-risk repair or unsupervised hazardous activity.
Instructions are clear to another household member.
The process includes stop/escalation triggers.
The change does not trade safety for speed.

rubric.process_understanding: 0–3: from vague to accurate sequence and constraints
rubric.risk_recognition: 0–3: from missed hazards to clear stop/escalation rules
rubric.quantitative_accuracy: 0–3: from absent to correct and relevant estimates
rubric.usability: 0–3: from unclear to tested and repeatable

projects.safety_ethics: Do not handle mains wiring, gas, chemicals, medication, sharp tools or heavy loads without qualified adult supervision; stop and escalate uncertainty.
projects.transfer_test: Use the same process-mapping method on a digital workflow and explain new cyber/privacy risks.

projects.title: Ethical micro-venture experiment with a real stop rule
projects.challenge: Evaluate a small lawful offer through a bounded, low-cost experiment without assuming sales prove long-term viability.
phases: Define a problem and offer without exaggerated claims.
Set a guardian-approved spending ceiling and no-debt rule.
Estimate costs, time, capacity and contribution margin.
Run a small transparent test with permission.
Reconcile every transaction and separate revenue from profit.
Decide to stop, change or continue based on evidence.
acceptance_criteria: No borrowing, speculative investment or misleading claims.
Cash records reconcile.
The metric and stop rule are defined before the test.
Negative results are reported honestly.

rubric.customer_evidence: 0–3: from assumption to bounded direct evidence
rubric.financial_control: 0–3: from unreconciled to accurate ledger and costs
rubric.experiment_design: 0–3: from vague to measurable with stop rule
rubric.ethics: 0–3: from risky/misleading to transparent and permission-based

projects.safety_ethics: For minors: guardian oversight, lawful age-appropriate activity, no debt, no high-risk financial products, no collection of unnecessary customer data.
projects.transfer_test: Use the experiment framework to test a non-commercial hypothesis and compare ethical constraints.

projects.title: Personal knowledge system with evidence and delayed recall
projects.challenge: Build a small offline-first knowledge collection that helps a learner retrieve and explain what they studied.
deliverables: simple data model and stable IDs
phases: Select a narrow topic and define what counts as a useful note.
Record source, author/publisher, access date and claim scope.
Create stable identifiers and explicit links.
Design retrieval prompts that require explanation, not recognition only.
Test navigation and accessibility on a phone.
Revisit after a delay and record corrections or gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Links resolve and IDs remain stable.
Source claims are distinguishable from learner inference.
Retrieval requires unaided explanation.
The system works without mandatory cloud access.

rubric.information_model: 0–3: from ad hoc to consistent and navigable
rubric.provenance: 0–3: from missing to traceable and qualified
rubric.retrieval_design: 0–3: from recognition-only to explanatory delayed recall
rubric.usability: 0–3: from fragile to phone-usable and resilient

projects.safety_ethics: Do not store passwords, identity numbers, private messages or sensitive personal records; backup and export must be understandable.
projects.transfer_test: Reuse the knowledge model for a different discipline and identify which metadata fields need domain-specific additions.

projects.title: Team challenge: plan, build, communicate and review
projects.challenge: A small team delivers a modest, safe community or school-facing artefact with clear roles and accountable review.
phases: Agree on purpose, roles, boundaries and decision rights.
Break work into testable tasks with owners and dependencies.
Create a prototype or performance with checkpoints.
Review accessibility, safety, privacy and permissions.
Demonstrate and collect structured feedback.
Run a retrospective that separates team outcome from individual learning.
acceptance_criteria: Roles and decisions are transparent.
No participant is pressured to share private information or perform unsafe tasks.
Deliverable meets stated user/audience criteria.
Each learner can explain their own contribution and a team trade-off.

rubric.coordination: 0–3: from unclear to accountable and adaptive roles
rubric.communication: 0–3: from opaque to clear and audience-aware
rubric.reflection: 0–3: from blame to evidence-based learning and responsibility

projects.safety_ethics: Obtain permission for public activity and images; use least-privilege access; avoid unsafe sport, tool or performance demands.
projects.transfer_test: Repeat with a different team composition and compare which coordination practices generalise.
